title: Primary Culture of Nodose Ganglion Neurons from Mouse
author: Diego DFF Fernández-Fernández
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kzxcx7n

steps.title: Prepare Sterilized Materials and Reagents
steps.instruction: Sterilize and maintain the following materials in a laminar flow cabinet, keeping them at 4ºC until use:

substeps.instruction: Corning wells (35 mm) and 10 mL tubes.
Two pasteur glass pipettes (one with a thin polished mouth, one with a broader mouth).
L-15 medium without L-glutamine.
HBSS + HEPES (10 mM final concentration of HEPES).
Culture medium: 50 mL L-15 supplemented with 10% foetal calf serum, 24 mM NaHCO3, 38 mM D-glucose, 100 UI/ml penicillin, 100 μg/ml streptomicyn, 2 mM L-glutamine, and 50 ng/ml nerve growth factor.
Trypsin: 1 mg/ml in HBSS + 6 mg/mL albumin.
Colagenase: 2.5 mg/ml in HBSS + 6 mg/ml albumin.
Laminin: Prepare 3 wells with 200 µL of laminin each (10 mg/ml solved in EBSS).

steps.title: Coat Wells with Laminin
steps.instruction: Incubate a drop of laminin in the prepared wells for at least two hours at 37ºC, 95% O2 / 5% CO2.

steps.title: Anaesthesise and Sacrifice Mouse
steps.instruction: Deeply anaesthesise a SWISS CD1 mouse (30-60 days old, male or female) using a CO2 chamber or isoflurane overdose.

substeps.instruction: Assess anaesthesia via foot pad pinch; apply further anaesthetic if the animal responds.
Quickly sacrifice the animal by decapitation.

steps.title: Extract Nodose Ganglia
steps.instruction: Extract the ganglia using autoclaved surgery material (kept in 70º alcohol when not in use, and washed in distilled water and saline (NaCl 0.9%) before use).

substeps.instruction: Position the animal backwards and pin.
Cut medially from the base of the neck to the mouth.
Pin the trachea to expose the nodose ganglion (enlargement of the vagus nerve parallel to the carotid artery).
Quickly isolate both bilateral ganglia by cutting them free from the vagus nerve.

steps.title: Initial Ganglia Cleaning
steps.instruction: Transfer both ganglia to a 35 mm well containing 1 mL of cold L-15 medium (Catalog #L4386).

substeps.instruction: Under magnification, clean both ganglia of remaining tissue, specifically blood.

steps.title: Enzymatic Dissociation
steps.instruction: Process the ganglia in a laminar flow cabinet to dissociate the neurons.

substeps.instruction: Wash ganglia 3 times with 2 mL of HBSS + HEPES.
Add 2 mL of colagenase solution and incubate for 15 minutes at 37ºC, 95% O2 / 5% CO2.
Wash twice with HBSS + HEPES to remove colagenase.
Add 2 mL of trypsin solution and incubate for 30 minutes at 37ºC, 95% O2 / 5% CO2.

steps.title: Mechanical Dissociation and Purification
steps.instruction: Complete the dissociation and isolate the neuronal pellet.

substeps.instruction: Transfer both ganglia with the minimum amount of trypsin into a 10 mL tube containing 2 mL medium (FCS stops trypsinization).
Using the small tip pasteur pipette, gently dissociate the ganglia until no longer visible.
Transfer the 3 mL cell suspension to another 10 mL tube containing 3 mL L-15.
Centrifuge the tube at 500 rpm for 3 minutes.
Carefully pour out the supernatant and add culture medium to the remaining white pellet of neurons.

steps.title: Prepare Wells for Seeding
steps.instruction: Prepare the laminin-coated wells while the cells are centrifuging.

substeps.instruction: Remove the laminin from the coated wells.
Wash the area where the laminin drop was at least 2 times with L-15.
Remove L-15 and leave the wells empty.

steps.title: Seed and Culture Neurons
steps.instruction: Seed the neurons and incubate for maturation.

substeps.instruction: Seed 200 µL (corrected from 'mL' based on context of 35mm wells) of medium + cell suspension in the center of each of the three wells.
Place wells in the incubator (95% O2 / 5% CO2) for 2 hours.
Carefully add 2 mL of non-cold culture medium to each well.
Maintain cells in the incubator (95% O2 / 5% CO2) for at least 24 hours before electrophysiological experiments.
